U.S. Representative Barry Loudermilk | Serving Georgia 11th District Follow Follow Follow Follow Follow Freedom, Security & Opportunity STAY CONNECTED: Subscribe to our Weekly Newsletter Subscribe Congressman Barry Loudermilk, a Constitutional Conservative, represents northwest Georgia’s 11th Congressional District. In the 119th Congress, Congressman Loudermilk serves as a member of the U.S. House Financial Services Committee and the Committee on House Administration. He also serves as the Chairman of the Select Subcommittee of the House Judiciary Committee and its investigation into the events at the Capitol on January 6, 2021. Additionally, he serves as a member of the Republican Study Committee (RSC), a conservative caucus of House Republicans. Read More A native of Georgia and veteran of the U.S. Air Force. A student of the Constitution and the Christian heritage of America. How Can I Help? My team and I serve our constituents in any way we can. Whether you need help with a federal agency, are trying to find out if federal grants are available for your project, or are considering applying to a service academy. We hope all the information in this section will be helpful. Help With A Federal Agency Email Rep. Issues | U.S. Representative Barry Loudermilk Top Priorities for America $ Defense Ensuring a strong national defense to protect our citizens and uphold American interests worldwide. $ Banking/Financial Services Promoting a stable, fair financial system that supports economic growth and protects consumers. $ Congressional Oversight Committed to transparency and accountability by holding government agencies and officials accountable. $ Agriculture Supporting policies that empower our farmers, protect rural communities, and ensure a safe, abundant food supply for all Americans. $ Budget and Spending Supporting a constitutional amendment to require the federal government to balance its budget and curb deficit spending. $ Article I Project Restoring the constitutional balance of power by reasserting Congress’s authority as outlined in Article I. $ Education Advocating for parental choice, local control, and reforms that prepare students for future success. $ Energy Our nation’s energy strategy must embrace domestic production and use emerging technologies that spark innovation. $ Health Care Supporting patient-centered reforms that improve access, lower costs, and enhance the quality of health care. $ Homeland Security & Immigration Strengthening our homeland security to protect Americans from threats at home and abroad as well as securing our borders, reforming immigration law and prioritizing American workers and taxpayers. $ MERIT Act Makes It easier to hold poor performing federal employees accountable. $ Military and Veterans Honoring our veterans and ensuring our military has the resources needed to defend our nation. $ Trade Working to create fair trade policies that protect American jobs, strengthen our economy, and uphold national interests. $ Supreme Court Defending the integrity of the Supreme Court and the rule of law through constitutional judicial appointments. $ Science, Space, and Technology Investing in research and innovation to keep America a global leader in space exploration and technology advancements. $ Values Ensuring that our American values are cherished and upheld, and we work to keep our nation free, safe, and full of opportunity.

Appropriations | U.S. Representative Barry Loudermilk Appropriations requests for FY 2027 October 1, 2026 – September 30, 2027 Thank you for your interest in the fiscal year 2027 appropriations process. If you are interested in submitting information pertaining to programmatic, report language, or community project funding requests, please fill out this form as completely as possible for each request that you want considered. There is no guarantee that the request will be supported. Early submissions are welcome and appreciated. General guidance for programmatic and language requests can be found HERE . IMPORTANT NOTE FOR COMMUNITY PROJECT FUNDING: Congressman Loudermilk’s office will consider requests for community project funding on a case-by-case basis. The Appropriations Committee has released its Fiscal Year 2027 appropriations guidance and deadlines for Community Project Funding, and they can be found HERE . Requests should include specific information on the project’s benefits to people throughout Georgia’s 11th Congressional District in Bartow, Cherokee, Cobb, Gordon, and Pickens Counties. Any questions on Community Project Funding should be directed to Ashleigh Padgett at Ashleigh.Padgett@mail.house.gov The Deadline for requests to be submitted to our office for consideration is March 11, 2026 . Staff contact for questions regarding each Appropriations Subcommittee can be found below.
